FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A36
A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle’s rear indicates travel below 25 miles per hour. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A36
The slow-moving emblem may appear on construction equipment, farm vehicles and horse-drawn wagons or carriages. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A36
Guide signs are square or rectangular and use green, brown or blue backgrounds. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A36
Guide signs identify intersecting roads, directions to communities, points of interest and nearby traveler services. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A36
A route-number sign’s shape and color indicate whether the road is interstate, United States, state, city, county or local. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A36
Plan a route with a map and follow route signs while traveling through unfamiliar areas. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A36
Service signs are blue squares or rectangles with white words or symbols. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A36
Service signs identify facilities such as rest areas, fuel stations, campgrounds and hospitals. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A36
Destination signs are green or brown squares or rectangles with white lettering. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A36
Destination signs give directions and distances to communities, airports, state boundaries and places of interest. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A36
Road markings use painted lines, arrows, words or symbols to give instructions or warnings. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A36
Pavement markings divide lanes and identify passing or lane changes, turn lanes, pedestrian crossings and stopping locations. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A36
The handbook’s double-yellow-line caption identifies a two-way road where passing is prohibited in both directions. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A36
On the pictured two-way-road arrangement, passing is allowed on the side with the dashed yellow line. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A36
The handbook labels a dashed-yellow-line two-way-road arrangement as allowing passing. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A36
The handbook labels dashed white lines on a one-direction road as allowing passing. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0036]

Misconceptions: An unmarked crosswalk still may exist; a shared center lane serves turning traffic from both directions; a passing marking does not remove other safety duties.
Mnemonics: Use color, line pattern, direction and permitted action as an authored cue.
Glossary: A stop line determines the first required stopping boundary; a shared center lane accommodates left turns and permitted U-turns; guide signs provide routing and services information.
Dynamic facts: Route numbers and local crosswalk layouts vary by location; no unobserved graphic or local route is invented.
